Having thusthus, in few wordswords, given you a taste of the sorrow and affliction that my Soulsoul went under, by the guilt and terror that this my wicked thought did lay me under; and having given you also a touch of my deliverance therefrom, and of the sweet and blessed comfort that I met with afterwards, (which comfort dwelt about a twelve monthtwelvemonth with my Heartheart, to my unspeakable admiration); I will now (, God willing), before I proceed any further, give you in a word or two, Whatwhat, as I conceive, was the cause of this temptation; and also after that, what advantageadvantage, at the lastlast, it became unto my Soulsoul.

238237. For the causes, I conceived they were principally two;: of which two also I was deeply convinced all the time this trouble lay upon me. The first was, for that I did not, when I was delivered from the temptation that went before, still pray to God to keep me from temptations that were to come; for though, as I can
say in truth, my Soulsoul was much in Prayerprayer before this tryaltrial seized me., Yetyet then I prayed only, or at the most, principally, for the removal of present troubles, and for fresh discoveries of hisHis love in Christ;, which I saw afterwards was not enough to do; I also should have prayed, that the great God would keep me from the evil that was to come.

239238. Of this I was made deeply sensible by the Prayerprayer of Holyholy David, whowho, when he was under present Mercymercy, yet prayed that God would hold him back from sin, and temptation to come: For; for ‘ then,,’ saith he,, ‘ shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the Greatgreat Transgressiontransgression,’ Psal(Ps. 161.9: 1313). By this very word was I gauledgalled and condemnedcondemned, quite through this long temptation.

240239. That also was another word that did much condemn me for my folly, in the neglect of this Dutyduty (Heb 4:16), Heb. 4. 16.‘ Let us therefore come boldly to the throne of Gracegrace, that we may obtain mercy, and find Gracegrace to help in time of need:.’ This I had not done, and therefore was thus suffered to sin and fall, according to what is written,, ‘ Pray that you enter not into temptation: and.’ And truly this very thing is to this day of such weight and awe upon me, that I dare not, when I come before the
Lord, go off my kneesknees, until I intreatentreat himHim for help and mercy against the temptations that are to come; and I do beseech thee, Readerreader, that thou learn to beware of my negligencenegligence, by the afflictions that for this thing I did for days, and months, and years, with sorrow undergo.

241240. Another cause of this temptation was, Thatthat I had tempted God; and on this manner did I do it:. Upon a time my Wifewife was great with Childchild, and before her full time was come, her pangspangs, as of a Womanwoman in Traveltravail, were fierce and strong upon her, even as if she would immediately have fallen in labour, and been delivered of an untimely Birthbirth:. NowNow, at this very time it was, that I had been so strongly tempted to question the Beingbeing of God;, wherefore, as my Wifewife lay crying by me, I said, but with all secresiesecrecysecresy imaginable, even thinking in my heart, Lord, if thouThou wilt now remove this sad affliction from my Wifewife, and cause that she be troubled no more therewith this Nightnight, (and now were her pangs just upon her), then I shall know that thouThou canst discern the most secret thoughts of the Heartheart.

242241. I had no sooner said it in my heart, but her pangs were taken from her, and she was cast into a deep sleep, and so continued
till Morningmorning; at this I greatly marvelled, not knowing what to think; but after I had been awake a good while, and heard her cry no more, I fell to sleep also;. So when I waked in the Morningmorning, it came upon me again, even what I had said in my heart the last Nightnight, and how the Lord had shewedshowed me that heHe knew my secret Thoughtsthoughts, which was a great astonishment unto me for several weeks after.

243242. Well, about a year and a half afterwardsafterwards, that wicked sinful thought, of which I have spoken before, went thorowthrough my wicked heart, even this thought, Let Christ go if heHe will; so when I was fallen under guilt for this, the remembrance of my other thought, and of the effect thereof, would also come upon me with this retort, which also carried rebuke along with it, Now you may see that God doth know the most secret thoughts of the Heartheart.

244243. And with this, that of the passages that were betwixt the Lord, and hisHis Servantservant Gideon, fell upon my Spiritspirit; how because that Gideon tempted God with his Fleecefleece, both wet and dry, when he should have believed and ventured upon his word, therefore the Lord did afterwards so try him,
as to send him against an innumerable company of Enemiesenemies.; Andand that tootoo, as to outward appearance, without any strength or help, ( Judg. 6.– 77). Thus heHe served me, and that justly, for I should have believed hisHis Wordword, and not have put an Ifif upon the Allall-seeingness of God.

245244. And now to shewshow you something of the advantages that I also have gained by this temptation; and first, byBy this I was made continually to possess in my Soulsoul a very wonderful sense both of the Beingbeing and Gloryglory of God, and of hisHis beloved Son; in the temptation that went before, my Soulsoul was perplexed with unbelief, blasphemy, hardness of Heartheart, questions about the Beingbeing of God, Christ, the Truthtruth of the Word, and certainty of the Worldworld to come; I say, then I was greatly assaulted, and tormented with Atheismatheism,; but now the case was otherwise, now was God and Christ continually before my Faceface, though not in a way of comfort, but in a way of exceeding dread and terror. The Gloryglory of the Holinessholiness of God did at this time break me to pieces,; and the Bowelsbowels and Compassioncompassion of Christ did break me as on the Wheelwheel; for I could not consider himHim but as a lost and rejected Christ, the
remembrance of which, was as the continual breaking of my Bonesbones.

246245. The Scriptures also were wonderful things unto me; I saw that the truth and verity of them, were the Keyskeys of the Kingdomkingdom of Heavenheaven; those that the Scriptures favour, they must inherit bliss;, but those that they oppose and condemn, must perish for evermore: O. Oh! this word,, ‘ For the Scriptures cannot be broken,,’ would rend the Caulcaul of my Heartheart?; andandAnd so would that other, W'hose‘Whose sins ye remit, they are remitted; but whose sins ye retain, they are retained:.’ Now I saw the Apostlesapostles to be the Elderselders of the Citycity of Refugerefuge (Josh 20:4), Josh. 20. 4. thosethoseThose that they were to receive in, were received to Lifelife?; butbutBut those that they shut out, were to be slain by the avenger of Bloodblood.

247246. Oh! Oneone Sentencesentence of the Scripture did more afflict and terrifieterrify my mind, I mean those Sentencessentences that stood against me (, as sometimes I thought they every one did), more, I saysay, than an Armyarmy of forty thousand men that might have come against me. Woe be to him against whom the Scriptures bend themselves.

248247. By this temptation I was made to see more into the Naturenature of the Promises,promises than ever I was before; for I lying now trembling
under the mighty hand of God, continually torn and rent by the thundering of hisHis Justicejustice; this made meme, with careful Heart,heart and watchful Eyeeye, with great fearfulness, to turn over every leaf, and with much diligencediligence, mixtmixed with trembling, to consider every Sentencesentence, together with its natural force and latitude.

249248. By this temptationtemptation, also, I was greatly holdenheld off my former foolish practice, of putting by the word of promise when it came into my mind; for now, though I could not suck that comfort and sweetness from the Promise,promise as I had done at other times, yet, like to a man aa- sinking, I should catch at all I saw; formerly I thought I might not meddle with the promise, unless I felt its comfort, but now’ twasnow it was no time thus to do, the avenger of Bloodblood too hardly did pursue me.

250249. Now therefore I was glad to catch at that word, which yet I feared, I had no ground nor right to own; and even to leap into the bosom of that promise, that yet I fear’dfeared did shut its Heartheart against me. Now also I should labour to take the Word as God hath laid it down, without restraining the natural force of one syllable thereof;. O what did I now see in that blessed sixth of John,, ‘ And him that comes to me, I will in no
wise cast outout’! ( Johnv. 6. 3037). Now I began to consider with my selfmyself, that God had a bigger mouth to speak with, than I had a heart to conceive with;. I thought also with my self,myself that heHe spake not hisHis words in haste, or in an unadvised heat, but with infinite Wisdomwisdom and Judgmentjudgment, and in very truth and faithfulness, ( 2 Sam. 3.: 2828).

251250. I should in these days, often in my greatest Agoniesagonies, even flounce towards the Promisepromise, (as the Horseshorses do towards sound Ground,ground that yet stick in the mire), concluding, (though as one almost bereft of his wits through fear), on this I will rest and stay, and leave the fulfilling of it to the God of Heavenheaven that made it. OOh! many a pull hath my heart had with Sathan,Satan for that blessed sixth of John;. I did not now, as at other times, look principally for comfort, (though, O how welcome would it have been unto me!) But now a word, a word to lean a weary Soulsoul upon, that I might not sink for ever!’ it twaswasTwas that I hunted for.

252251. Yea, often when I have been making to the Promisepromise, I have seen as if the Lord would refuse my Soulsoul for ever;. I was often as if I had run upon the Pikespikes, and as if the Lord had thrust at me, to keep me from him,Him as with a flaming Swordsword. Then
I should think of Esther, who went to petition the Kingking contrary to the Lawlaw, ( Esth. 4.: 1616). I thought also of Benhadad’s Servantsservants, who went with Ropesropes upon their Headsheads to their Enemiesenemies for mercy, ( 1 KingKg.s 20.: 31. &etc)c. The Womanwoman of Canaan also, that would not be daunted, though called Dogdog by Christ, Mat. (Matt 15. 22. &etcc. andAnd:21–28); and the man that went to borrow bread at Midnightmidnight (Luke 11:5–8), Luke 1. 5, 6, 7, 8, &etcc. wereWerewere great encouragements unto me.

253252. I never saw those heights and depths in Grace and Lovegrace, and Mercylove, and mercy, as I saw after this temptation!. Great Sinssins do draw out great Gracegrace; and where guilt is most terrible and fierce, there the mercy of God in Christ, when shewedshowed to the Soulsoul, appears most high and mighty;. whenWhen Job had passed through his Captivitycaptivity, he hadhad ‘ twice as much as he had beforebefore’, ( Job. 42.: 1010). Blessed be God for Jesus Christ our Lord. Many other things I might here make observation of, but I would be brief, and therefore shall at this time omit them, and do pray God that my harms may make others fear to offend, lest they also be made to bear the Ironiron Yokeyoke as I did.

I had two or three times, at or about my deliverance from this temptationtemptation, such strange apprehensions of the Gracegrace of God, that I
could hardly bear up under it, it was so out of measure amazing, when I thought it could reach me, that I do think, if that sense of it had abode long upon me, it would have made me uncapableincapable for business.

254253. Now I shall go forward to give you a relation of other of the LordsLord’s dealings with me,, of His dealings with me at sundry other seasons, and of the temptations I then did meet withal. I shall begin with what I met with when I first did joynjoin in fellowship with the Peoplepeople of God in Bedford. After I had propounded to the Church,church that my desire was to walk in the Orderorder and Ordinancesordinances of Christ with them, and was also admitted by them:; while I thought of that blessed Ordinanceordinance of Christ, which was hisHis last Suppersupper with hisHis Disciplesdisciples before hisHis death, that Scripturescripture,, ‘ Do this in remembrance of meme’, ( Luke 22.: 19. wasWas), was made a very precious word unto me:; for by it the Lord. didDid did come down upon my Conscienceconscience with the discovery of hisHis death for my sins,; and as I then felt, did as if heHe plunged me in the vertuevirtue of the same. But, behold, I had not been long a partaker at that Ordinanceordinance, but such fierce and sad temptations did attend me at all times therein, both to blaspheme the Ordinanceordinance, and to wish some deadly thing to those that then did eat thereof:; thatthat, lest
I should at any time be guilty of consenting to these wicked and fearful thoughts, I was forced to bend my self,myself all the while to pray to God to keep me from such Blasphemiesblasphemies:; and also to cry to God to bless the Breadbread and Cupcup to them, as it went from mouth to mouth. The reason of this temptation I have thought since, was, because I did notnot, with that reverence as became meme, at first, approach to partake thereof.

255254. Thus I continued for threethree- quarters of a Yearyear, and could never have rest nor ease:; but at the last the Lord came in upon my Soulsoul with that same Scripture,scripture by which my Soulsoul was visited before:; and after that, I have been usually very well and comfortable in the partaking of that blessed Ordinanceordinance, and have, I trust, therein discerned the LordsLord’s Bodybody as broken for my sins, and that hisHis precious blood hath been shed for my Transgressionstransgressions.

256255. Upon a time I was somewhat inclining to a Consumptionconsumption, wherewithwherewith, about the Springspring, I was suddenly and violently seized, with much weakness in my outward man:, insomuch that I thought I could not live. Now began I afresh to give my selfmyself up to a serious examination after my state and condition for the future, and of my evidences
for that blessed Worldworld to come; Forfor it hath, I bless the name of God, been my usual course, as always, so especially in the day of affliction, to endeavour to keep my interest in Lifelife to come, clear before minemy Eyeeye.

257256. But I had no sooner began to recall to mind my former experience, of the goodness of God to my Soulsoul, but there came flocking into my mind, an innumerable company of my Sinssins and Transgressionstransgressions, amongst which these were at this time most to my Afflictionaffliction, namelynamely, my deadness, dulness, and coldness in holy Dutiesduties; my wanderings of heart, of my wearisomnelswearisomeness in all good things, my want of love to God, hisHis waysways, and Peoplepeople, with this at the end of all, Are these the fruits of Christianity? Areare these the tokens of a blessed man?

258257. At the apprehensions of these things my sickness was doubled upon me, for now was I sick in my inward man, my Soulsoul was clog’dclogged with guilt; now also was all my former experience of God’s goodness to me, quite taken out of my mind, and hid as if they had never been, nor seen:. Now was my Soulsoul greatly pinched between these two considerations,. Live I must not, Die I dare not; Nownow I sunk and fell in my spirit,; and was
giving up all for lost; but as I was walking up and down in the househouse, as a man in a most wofulwoeful state, that Wordword of God took hold of my heart., Ye areare ‘ justified freely by his Gracegrace, through the Redemptionredemption that is in Christ JesusJesus’, ( Rom. 3.: 2424). But ohoh, what a turn it made upon me!

259258. Now was I as one awaked out of some troublesome sleep and dream, and listening to this Heavenlyheavenly Sentencesentence, I was as if I heard it thus expounded to me;: Sinner, thou thinkest that because of thy Sinssins and Infirmities,infirmities I cannot save thy Soulsoul;, but behold, my My Son is by meMe, and upon himHim I look, and not on thee, and will deal with thee according as I am pleased with himHim. At this I was greatly lightnedlightened in my Mindmind, and made to understand that God could justifiejustify a sinner at any time,; it was but hisHis looking upon Christ, and imputing of hisHis benefits to us, and the work was forthwith done.

260259. And as I was thus in a muse, that Scripturescripture also came with great power upon my Spiritspirit,, ‘ Not by works of Righteousnessrighteousness that we have done, but according to his Mercymercy he hath saved us,,’ &etcc.. (Titus 3:5; 2 Tim. 1.: 9. Tit. 3. 5). Now was I got on high,; I saw my selfmyself within the Armsarms of Gracegrace and mercy,; and though I was before afraid to think of a dying hour,
yet now I cryedcried, Let me die:. nowNow Deathdeath was lovely and beautiful in my sight,; for I saw we shall never live indeed till we be gone to the other Worldworld. OOh, methought this Lifelife is but a slumber, in comparison of that above; at this time also I saw more in those words,, ‘ Heirs of God,God’ (Rom. 8.: 17.) then, than ever I shall be able to express while I live in this World;world. ‘ Heirs of GodGod’! God himselfHimself is the portion of the Saintssaints. This I saw and wondered at, but cannot tell you what I saw.

261260. Again, as I was at another time very ill and weak, all that time also the Temptertempter did beset me strongly, (for I find he is much for assaulting the Soul,soul when it begins to approach towards the Gravegrave, then is his Opportunityopportunity), labouring to hide from me my former experience of GodsGod’s goodness; Alsoalso setting before me the terrors of Death,death and the Judgmentjudgment of God, insomuch, that at this time, through my fear of miscarrying for ever (, should I now die), I was as one dead before Deathdeath came, and was as if I had felt my selfmyself already descending into the Pitpit; methought, I saidsaid, there werewas no wayway, but to Hellhell I must; but behold, just as I was in the midst of those fears, these words of the Angelsangels carrying Lazarus into AbrahamsAbraham’s bosom, darted in upon me, as who should say, So it
shall be with thee, when thou dost leave this Worldworld. This did sweetly revive my Spiritspirit, and help me to hope in God; whichwhich, when I had with comfort mused on a while, that word fell with great weight upon my mind,, ‘ O Deathdeath, where is thy sting,? O Gravegrave, where is thy victory??’ ( 1 Cor 15.: 5555). At this I became both well in body and mind at once, for my sickness did presently vanish, and I walked comfortably in my Workwork for God again.

262261. At another time, though, just before, I was pretty well and savoury in my Spiritspirit, yet suddenly there fell upon me a great cloud of darkness, which did so hide from me the things of God and Christ, that I was as if I had never seen or known them in my life:; I was also so over-runoverrun in my Soulsoul, with a senslesssenseless, heartless frame of Spiritspirit, that I could not feel my Soulsoul to move or stir after Gracegrace and Lifelife by Christ; I was as if my loynsloins were broken, or as if my hands and feet had been tied or bound with Chainschains. At this time also I felt some weakness to seize upon my outward man, which made still the other affliction the more heavy and uncomfortable to me.

263262. After I had been in this condition some three or four days, as I was sitting by the fire, I suddenly felt this Wordword to sound
in my Heartheart, I must go to Jesus; at this my former darkness and Atheismatheism fled away, and the blessed things of Heavenheaven were set within my view. While I was on this sudden thus overtaken with surprizesurprise;, Wife, said I, is there ever such a Scripturescripture, I must go to Jesus? sheShe said she could not tell;, therefore I sat musing still to see if I could remember such a place; I had not sat above two or three minutes, but that came bolting in upon me,, ‘ And to an innumerable Companycompany of Angelsangels;,’ and withal, Hebrews the twelfth, about the Mountmount SionSion, was set before mine Eyeseyes, Heb. 12(vv. 22, 23,– 2424).

264263. Then with Joyjoy I told my Wifewife, O now I know, I know! butBut that night was a good night to me, I never had but few better:; I longed for the company of some of God’s People,people that I might have imparted unto them what God had shewedshowed me;. Christ was a precious Christ to my Soulsoul that Nightnight,; I could scarce lie in my Bedbed for Joyjoy, and Peacepeace, and Triumphtriumph, through Christ; this great Gloryglory did not continue upon me until Morningmorning, yet the twelfth of the Authorauthor to the Hebrews, ( Heb. 12.: 22,– 2324.) waswasWas a blessed Scripturescripture to me for many days together after this.

265264. The Wordswords are these,, ‘ You are come to Mountmount Sion, to the Citycity of the living God, to the Heavenlyheavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of Angelsangels, to the general Assemblyassembly and Churchchurch of the firstfirstborn born, which are written in Heavenheaven, to God the Judge of all, and to the Spiritsspirits of just men made perfect, and to Jesus the Mediatormediator of the Newnew Testament, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel. Thorow’ Through this blessed Sentence,sentence the Lord led me over and over, first to this Wordword, and then to that, and shewedshowed me wonderful glory in every one of them. These words also have oft since this time been great refreshment to my Spiritspirit. Blessed be God for having mercy on meme.

div.head: A brief Account of the Authors Call to the Work of the Ministry.
div.p:
266265. ANDAnd now I am speaking my Experienceexperience, I will in this place thrust in a word or two concerning my Preachingpreaching the Word, and of God’s dealing with me in that particular also:. For after I had been about five or six years awakened, and helped
my selfmyself to see both the want and worth of Jesus Christ our Lord, and also inabledenabled to venture my Soulsoul upon himHim:, some of the most able among the Saintssaints with us, I say, the most able for Judgment,judgment and Holinessholiness of Lifelife, as they conceived, did perceive that God had counted me worthy to understand something of hisHis Willwill in hisHis holy and blessed Word, and had given me utteranceutterance, in some measuremeasure, to express what I saw, to others for edification; therefore they desired me, and that with much earnestness, that I would be willingwilling, at somesometimes times, to take in hand, in one of the Meetingsmeetings, to speak a word of Exhortationexhortation unto them..

267266. The which, though at the first it did much dash and abash my Spiritspirit, yet being still by them desired and intreatedentreated, I consented to their request, and did twice at two several Assembliesassemblies, (but in private), though with much weakness and infirmity, discover my Giftgift amongst them; at which they not only seemed to be, but did solemnly protest, as in the sight of the great God, they were both affected audand comforted, and gave thanks to the Father of Merciesmercies for the grace bestowed on me.

268267. After this, sometimes when some of them did go into the Countrycountry to teach, they
would also that I should go with them; wherewhere, though as yet I did not, nor durst not, make use of my Giftgift in an open way, yet more privately still, as I came amongst the good Peoplepeople in those places, I did sometimes speak a word of Admonitionadmonition unto them also; the whichwhich, they as the otherother received, received with re joycingrejoicing at the mercy of God to me-wardward, professing their Soulssouls were edified thereby.

269268. Wherefore, to be brief, at last, being still desired by the Churchchurch, after some solemn Prayerprayer to the Lord, with fasting, I was more particularly called forth, and appointed to a more ordinary and publickpublic Preachingpreaching the Word, not only toto, and amongst them that believed, but also to offer the Gospelgospel to those that had not yet received the Faithfaith thereof; Aboutabout which time I did evidently find in my Mindmind a secret pricking forward theretothereto; though, I bless God, not for desire of vain Gloryglory, for at that time I was most sorely afflicted with the fiery darts of the Devil,devil concerning my Eternaleternal Statestate.

270269. But yet could not be content, unless I was found in the Exerciseexercise of my Giftgift, unto which also I was greatly animated, not only by the continual desires of the Godlygodly, but also by that saying of Paul to the Corinthians,, ‘ I beseech you, Brethren,brethren (ye know the household
of StephanusStephanas, that it is the first fruitsfirstfruits of Achaia, and that they have addicted themselves to the Ministryministry of the Saintssaints)), that you submit your selvesyourselves unto such, and to every one that helpeth with us, and labourethlaboureth’, ( 1 Cor. 16.: 15, 1616).

271270. By this Texttext I was made to see that the Holy Ghost never intended that men who have Giftsgifts and Abilities,abilities should bury them in the earth, but rather did command and stir up such to the Exerciseexercise of their Giftgift, and also did commend those that were apt and ready so to do,, ‘ They have addicted themselves to the Ministryministry of the Saintssaints:.’ This Scripturescripture, in these daysdays, did continually run in my mindmind, to incourageencourage me, and strengthen me in this my work for God; I have been also incouragedencouraged from several other Scripturesscriptures and Examplesexamples of the Godlygodly, both specified in the Word and other ancient Historieshistories, ( Acts 8.: 4. andAnd; 18.: 24, 25. &etcc.; 1 Pet. 4.: 10.; Rom. 12.: 6.; FoxFoxe’s Acts and MonMonuments).

272271. Wherefore, though of my self,myself of all the Saintssaints the most unworthy, yet I, but with great fear and trembling at the sight of my own weakness, did set upon the work, and did according to my Giftgift, and the proportion of my Faithfaith, Preachpreach that blessed Gospelgospel that God had shewedshowed me in the Holyholy Word
of Truth: Whichtruth; which, when the Countrycountry understood, they came in to hear the Word by hundreds, and that from all parts, though upon sundry and divers accounts.

273272. And I thank God, he He gave unto me some measure of bowels audand pity for their Soulssouls, which also did put me forward to labour with great diligence and earnestnessearnestness, to find out such a word as might, if God would bless, lay hold of, and awaken the Conscienceconscience, in which also the good Lord had respect to the desire of hisHis Servantservant; for I had not preached long, before some began to be touchedtouched by the Word, and to be greatly afflicted in their Mindsminds at the apprehension of the greatness of their Sinsin, and of their need of Jesus Christ.

274273. But I at first could not believe that God should speak by me to the heart of any man, still counting my selfmyself unworthy,; yet those who thus were touched would love me and have a peculiar respect for me; and though I did put it from me, that they should be awakened by me, still they would confess it, and affirm it before the Saintssaints of God; they would also bless God for me (, unworthy Wretchwretch that I am!) and count me God’s Instrumentinstrument that shewedshowed to them the way of Salvationsalvation.

275274. WhereforeWherefore, seeing them in both their words and deeds to be so constant, and also in their Heartshearts so earnestly pressing after the knowledge of Jesus Christ, rejoycingrejoicing that ever God did send me where they were; then I began to conclude it might be so, that God had owned in hisHis Workwork such a foolish one as I;, and then came that Wordword of God to my heart with much sweet refreshment,, ‘ The blessing of them that were ready to perish is come upon me; yea, I caused the Widowswidow’s heart to sing for joyjoy’. ( Job. 29.: 1313).

276275. At this therefore I rejoiced, yea, the tears of those whom God did awaken by my Preaching,preaching would be both solace and encouragement to me; for I thought on those Sayingssayings,, ‘ Who is he that maketh me glad, but the same that is made sorry by me??’ ( 2 Cor. 2.: 2. And); and again, ThoughThough ‘ I be not an Apostleapostle to others, yet doubtless I am unto you,: for the Sealseal of my Apostleshipapostleship are ye in the LordLord’, ( 1 Cor. 6. 9: 22). These thingsthings, thereforetherefore, were as another Argumentargument unto me that God had called me to, and stood by me in this Workwork.

277276. In my Preachingpreaching of the Word, I took special notice of this one thing, namely That, that the Lord did lead me to begin where hisHis Word begins with Sinnerssinners,; that is, to condemn all flesh, and to open and alledgeallege
that the curse of GodGod, by the Lawlaw, doth belong to, and lay hold on all men as they come into the Worldworld, because of Sinsin. Now this part of my Workwork I fulfilled with great sense,; for the terrors of the Lawlaw, and guilt for my Transgressionstransgressions, lay heavy on my Conscienceconscience,. I preached what I felt, what I smartingly did feel, even that under which my poor Soulsoul did groan and tremble to astonishment.

278277. Indeed I have been as one sent to them from the dead; I went my selfmyself in Chainschains to preach to them in Chainschains,; and carried that fire in my own Conscience,conscience that I perswadedpersuaded them to beware of. I can truly say, and that without dissembling, that when I have been to preach, I have gone full of guilt and terror even to the Pulpit-pulpit door, and there it hath been taken off, and I have been at liberty in my mind until I have done my Workwork;, and then immediately, even before I could get down the Pulpit-pulpit stairs, I have been as bad as I was before.; Yetyet God carried me on, but surely with a strong hand;, for neither Guiltguilt nor Hellhell could take me off my Workwork.

279278. Thus I went for the space of two years, crying out against mensmen’s sins, and their fearful state because of them. After which,
the Lord came in upon my own Soulsoul with some staid peace and comfort through Christ; for heHe did give me many sweet discoveries of hisHis Blessedblessed Gracegrace thorowthrough himHim;. Wherefore now I altered in my preaching, (for still I preached what I saw and felt); now therefore I did much labour to hold forth Jesus Christ in all hisHis Officesoffices, Relationsrelations, and Benefitsbenefits unto the Worldworld,; and did strive also to discover, to condemn, and remove those false supports and props on which the Worldworld doth both lean, and by them fall and perish. On these things also I staid as long as on the other.

280279. After this, God led me into something of the Mysterymystery of the Unionunion of Christ; wherefore that I discovered and shewedshowed to them also. And when I had travelled through these three chief points of the Word of God, about the space of five years or more, I was caught in my present practice, and cast into Prisonprison, where I have lain above as long againagain, to confirm the Truthtruth by way of suffering, as I was before in testifying of it, according to the Scriptures, in a way of Preachingpreaching.

281280. When I have been in Preachingpreaching, I thank God, my heart hath often, all the time of this and the other exercise, with great earnestness
cryed, cried to God that heHe would make the Word effectual to the Salvationsalvation of the Soulsoul; still being grieved lest the Enemyenemy should take the Word away from the Conscienceconscience, and so it should become unfruitful;. Wherefore I should labour so to speak the Word, as that thereby (, if it were possible), the sin and Personperson guilty might be particularized by it.

282281. AlsoAlso, when I have done the Exerciseexercise, it hath gone to my heart to think the Word should now fall as Rainrain on stony places;, still wishing from my heart, O that they who have heard me speak this day, did but see as I dodo what sin, what Sindeath, Death, Hellhell, and the Cursecurse of God, is; and also what the Gracegrace, and Lovelove, and Mercymercy of God is, thorowthrough Christ, to men in such a case as they are, who are yet estranged from himHim. AndAnd, indeed, I did often say in my heart before the Lord, That if to be hanged up presently before their Eyes,eyes would be a means to awaken them, and confirm them in the Truthtruth, I gladly should be contented.

283282. For I have been in my Preachingpreaching, especially when I have been engaged in the Doctrinedoctrine of Lifelife by Christ, without Worksworks, as if an Angelangel of God had stood by at my back to encourage me;. OOh, it hath been with
such Powerpower and heavenly Evidenceevidence upon my own Soulsoul, while I have been labouring to unfold it, to demonstrate it, and to fasten it upon the Conscienceconscience of others, that I could not be contented with saying, I believebelieve, and am sure; methought I was more than sure (, if it be lawful to express my self)myself, that those things which then I asserted, were true.

284283. When I went first to Preachpreach the Word abroad, the Doctorsdoctors and Priestspriests of the Countrycountry did open wide against me;. butBut I was perswadedpersuaded of this, not to render railing for raylingrailing, but to see how many of their carnal Professorsprofessors I could convince of their miserable state by the Lawlaw, and of the want and worth of Christ; for, thought I, This shall answer for me in time to come, when they shall be for my hire before their face, ( Gen. 30.: 3333).

285284. I never cared to meddle with things that were controverted, and in dispute amongst the Saintssaints, especially things of the lowest Naturenature; yet it pleased me much to contend with great earnestness for the Wordword of Faith,faith and the Remissionremission of Sinssins by the Deathdeath and Sufferingssufferings of Jesus; but I say, as to other things, I should let them alone, because I saw they engendredengendered strife, and because that they neitherneither, in doing, nor in leaving
undone, did commend us to God to be hisHis:. Besides, I saw my Workwork before me did run in another Channelchannel, even to carry an awakening word; to that therefore did I stick and adhere.

285. I never endeavoured to, nor durst make use of other mensmen’s lineslines (Rom 15:18), Rom. 15. 18. (though I condemn not all that do), for I verily thought, and found by experience, that what was taught me by the Word and Spirit of Christ, could be spoken, maintainedmaintained, and stood to, by the soundest and best established Conscienceconscience; and though I will not now speak all that I know in this matter;, yet my experience hath more interest in that Texttext of Scripture, Gal. 1. 11, 12. thanthanThan many amongst men are awareaware (Gal 1:11, 12).

287286. If any of those who were awakened by my Ministry,ministry did after that fall back, (as sometimes too many did), I can truly say their loss hath been more to me, then than if one of my own Childrenchildren, begotten of my body, had been going to its Gravegrave; I thinkthink, verilyverily, I may speak it without any offence to the Lord, nothing hath gone so near me as that, unless it was the fear of the loss of the Salvationsalvation of my own Soulsoul:. I have counted as if I had goodly Buildingsbuildings and Lordshipslordships in those places where my Childrenchildren
were born:; my heart hath been so wraptwrapped up in the glory of this excellent Workwork, that I counted my selfmyself more blessed and honoured of God by this, than if heHe had made me the EmperouremperorEmperor of the Christian Worldworld, or the Lordlord of all the glory of the Earthearth without it! O these words!, ‘ He that converteth a Sinnersinner from the error of his way, doth save a Soulsoul from death, Jamdeath’ (Jas 5:20). 5. 20.‘ The fruit of the Righteous,righteous is a Treetree of Lifelife; and he that winneth Souls,souls is wisewise’, ( ProvProv 11:30). 11. 30.‘ They that be wise, shall shine as the brightness of the Firmamentfirmament,; and they that turn many to Righteousnessrighteousness, as the Starsstars for ever and everever’, ( DanDan 12:3). 12. 3.‘ For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of rejoicing? areAre not even ye in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming? forFor, ye are our glory and joyjoy’, ( 1 Thes.Thess 2.: 19, 2020). These, I say, with many others of a like nature, have been great refreshments to me.

288287. I have observed, Thatthat where I have had a Workwork to do for God, I have had firstfirst, as it werewere, the going of God upon my Spiritspirit to desire I might preach there:. I have also observed, that such and such Soulssouls in particular have been strongly set upon my heart, and I stirred up to wish for their Salvationsalvation; and that these very Soulssouls have, after this, been given in as the fruits of my Ministryministry.
I have observed, that a Wordword cast in by the by, hath done more execution in a Sermon,sermon than all that was spoken besides:; sometimes also when I have thought I did no good, then I did most of all; and at other times when I thought I should catchtcatch them, I have fished for nothing.

289288. I have also observed, that where there hath been a Workwork to do upon Sinnerssinners, there the Devildevil hath begun to roar in the hearts, and by the mouths of his Servantsservants. Yea, oftentimes when the wicked Worldworld hath raged most, there hath been Soulssouls awakened by the Wordword:. I could instance particulars, but I forbear.

290289. My great desire in my fulfilling my Ministry,ministry was, to get into the darkest places of the Countrycountry, even amongst those Peoplepeople that were furthest off of profession; yet not because I could not endure the Lightlight, (for I feared not to shewshow my Gospelgospel to any), but because I found my Spiritspirit did lean most after awakening and converting - Workwork, and the Word that I carried did lean it selfitself most that way also; Yea‘yea, so have I strived to preach the Gospelgospel, not where Christ was named, lest I should build upon another man's Foundationman’s foundation’ ( Rom. 15.: 2020).

291290. In my preaching, I have really been in pain, and have, as it were, travelledtravailed to bring forth Childrenchildren to God,; neither could I be satisfied, unless some fruits did appear in my Workwork:. ifIf I were fruitless, it mattered not who commended me; but if I were fruitful, I cared not who did condemn. I have thought of that,, ‘He that winneth souls is wise’ (Prov 11:30); and again, ‘ Lo, Childrenchildren are an Heritageheritage of the Lord; and the fruit of the Wombwomb is his reward. As Arrowsarrows in the hand of a mighty man, so are Childrenchildren of the Youthyouth. Happy is the man that hath filled his Quiverquiver full of them; they shall not be ashamed, but they shall speak with the Enemiesenemies in the Gategate,’ Psal(Ps. 127.: 3, 4,– 55).

292291. It pleased me nothing to see Peoplepeople drink in Opinions,opinions if they seemed ignorant of Jesus Christ, and the worth of their own Salvationsalvation, sound conviction for Sinsin, especially for Unbeliefunbelief, and an heart set on fire to be saved by Christ, with strong breathings after a truly sanctified Soulsoul:; that it was that delighted me; those were the Soulssouls I counted blessed.

293292. But in this Workwork, as in all other, I had my temptations attending me, and that of diversdiverse kinds, as sometimes I should be assaulted with great discouragement therein, fearing that I should not be able to speak a
wordWord at all to edification; nay, that I should not be able to speak sense unto the people; at which times I should have such a strange faintness and strengthlessness seize upon my body, that my legs have scarce been able to carry me to the place of Exerciseexercise.

294293. SometimesSometimes, again, when I have been preaching, I have been violently assaulted with thoughts of blasphemy, and strongly tempted to speak the words with my mouth before the Congregationcongregation. I have also at some time, even when I have begun to speak the Word with much clearness, evidence, and liberty of speech, yet been before the ending of that Opportunity,opportunity so blinded, and so estranged from the things I have been speaking, and have also been so straitnedstraitened in my speech, as to utterance before the Peoplepeople, that I have been as if I had not known or remembredremembered what I have been about, or, as if my head had been in a bag all the time of the Exerciseexercise.

295294. Again, Whenwhen at sometimes I have been about to Preachpreach upon some smart and searching portion of the Word, I have found the Temptertempter suggest, What!, willwillWill you preach this? thisthisThis condemns your selfyourself,; of this your own Soulsoul is guilty; wherefore preach not of it at all,; or if you do, yet so mince it, as to make way
for your own escape; lest instead of awakening others, you lay that guilt upon your own Soulsoul, as you will never get from under.

296295. But, I thank the Lord., I have been kept from consenting to these so horrid suggestions, and have rather, as SampsonSamson, bowed my selfmyself with all my mightmight, to condemn Sinsin and Transgression where evertransgression wherever I found it, yeayea, though therein also I did bring guilt upon my own Conscience;conscience! ‘ Let me dyedie,,’ thought I,, ‘ with the PhilistinesPhilistines’, ( Judg. 16.: 29, 30. ratherRather), rather than deal corruptly with the blessed Word of God;, ‘ Thou that teachest another, teachest thou not thy selfthyself??’ itIt is far better that thou do judge thy selfthyself, even by preaching plainly unto others, thenthan that thou, to save thy selfthyself, imprison the Truthtruth in Unrighteousnessunrighteousness:; Blessedblessed be God for hisHis help also in this.

297296. I have also, while found in this blessed work of Christ, been often tempted to pride and liftings up of Heartheart; and though I dare not say, I have not been affected with this, yet truly the LordLord, of hisHis precious mercymercy, hath so carried it towards me, thatthat, for the most partpart, I have had but small joy to give way to such a thing:; for it hath been my every daysday’s portion to be let into the evil of my own heart, and still made to see such
a multitude of Corruptionscorruptions and Infirmitiesinfirmities therein, that it hath caused hanging down of the head under all my Giftsgifts and Attainmentsattainments; I have felt this Thornthorn in the Fleshflesh (2 Cor. 12. 8, 9,) the very Mercymercy of God to meme (2 Cor 12:7–9).

298297. I have had alsoalso, together with thisthis, some notable place or other of the Word presented before me, which word hath contained in it some sharp and piercing Sentencesentence concerning the perishing of the Soulsoul, notwithstanding gifts and parts; asas, for instance, that hath been of great use unto me,, ‘ Though I speak with the Tonguetongue of Menmen and Angelsangels, and have not Charitycharity, I am become as sounding brass, and a tinkling Cymbalcymbal’, ( 1 Cor. 13.: 1, 22).

299298. A tinkling Cymbal,cymbal is an Instrumentinstrument of Musickmusic, with which a skilful Playerplayer can make such melodious and heart-inflaming Musickmusic, that all who hear him play, can scarcely hold from dancing; and yet behold, the Cymbalcymbal hath not Lifelife, neither comes the Musickmusic from it, but because of the Artart of him that plays therewith,; so then the Instrumentinstrument at last may come to naught and perish, thoughthough, in times pastpast, such Musickmusic hath been made upon it.

300299. Just thus, I saw, it was and will be with them who have Giftsgifts, but want saving -
Grace;grace, they are in the hand of Christ, as the Cymbalcymbal in the hand of David; and as David couldcould, with the Cymbalcymbal, make that Mirthmirth in the Serviceservice of God, as to elevate the hearts of the Worshippersworshippers, so Christ can use these gifted men, as with them to affect the Soulssouls of hisHis Peoplepeople in hisHis Churchchurch; yet when heHe hath done all, hang them by, as lifeless, though sounding Cymbalscymbals.

301300. This considerationconsideration, therefore, together with some others, were, for the most part, as a Maulmaul on the head of Pridepride, and desire of vain -glory:; Whatwhat, thought I, shall I be proud because I am a sounding Brassbrass? Is it so much to be a Fiddlefiddle? Hath not the least Creaturecreature that hath life, more of God in it than these? BesidesBesides, I knew’ twas Loveknew it was love should never die, but these must cease and vanish:; Soso I concluded, a little Gracegrace, a little Lovelove, a little of the true Fearfear of GodGod, is better than all these Giftsgifts:; Yeayea, and I am fully convinced of it, that it is possible for Soulssouls that can scarce give a man an answer, but with great confusion as to method, I say, it is possible for them to have a thousand times more Gracegrace, and so to be more in the love and favour of the Lord, than some whowho, by vertuevirtue of the Giftgift of Knowledgeknowledge, can deliver themselves like Angelsangels.

302301. ThusThus, thereforetherefore, I came to perceive, that though gifts in themselves were good to the thing for which they are designed, to wit, the Edificationedification of others,; yet empty and without power to save the Soulsoul of him that hath them, if they be alone:; Neitherneither are they, as so, any sign of a mansman’s state to be happy, being only a dispensation of God to some, of whose improvementimprovement, or non-improvementimprovement, they mustmust, when a little love more is over, give an account to himHim that is ready to judge the quick and the dead.

303302. This shewedshowed meme, too, that gifts being alone, were dangerous, not in themselves, but because of those evils that attend them that have them, to wit, pride, desire of vain glory, self-conceit, &etcc. all, all ofAll which were easily blown up at the applause, and commendation of every unadvised Christian, to the endangering of a poor Creaturecreature to fall into the condemnation of the Devildevil.

304303. I saw therefore that he that hath Gifts,gifts had need be let into a sight of the nature of them, to wit, that they come short of making of him to be in a truly saved condition, lest he rest in them, and so fall short of the grace of God.

305304. He hath also cause to walk humbly with God, and be little in his own Eyeseyes, and
to remember withallwithal, that his Giftsgifts are not his own, but the Churcheschurch’s,; and that by them he is made a Servantservant to the Churchchurch,; and he must also give at last an account of his Stewardshipstewardship unto the Lord Jesus,; and to give a good account, will be a blessed thing!.

306305. Let all men therefore prize a little with the fear of the Lord, (Gifts; gifts indeed are desirable), but yet great Gracegrace and small Giftsgifts are better thenthan great Giftsgifts and no Gracegrace. It doth not say, the Lord gives Giftsgifts and Gloryglory, but the Lord gives Gracegrace and Gloryglory!; andandAnd blessed is such an one; to whom the Lord gives Gracegrace, true Gracegrace, for that is a certain forerunner of Gloryglory.

307306. But when Satan perceived that his thus tempting and assaulting of me would not answer his design;, to wit, to overthrow my Ministryministry, and make it ineffectualineffectual, as to the ends thereof:; then he tryedtried another way, which was, to stir up the minds of the ignorant, and malicious, to load me with slanders and reproaches; now therefore I may say, Thatthat what the Devildevil could devise, and his instruments invent, was whirled up and down the Countrycountry against me, thinking, as I said, that by that means they should make my Ministryministry to be abandoned.
308307. It began therefore to be rumoredrumoured up and down among the Peoplepeople, that I was a Witchwitch, a Jesuit, a High-way-manhighwayman, and the like.

309308. To all which, I shall only say, God knows that I am innocent. But as for mine accusers, let them provide themselves to meet me before the Tribunaltribunal of the Son of God, there to answer for all these things (, with all the rest of their Iniquitiesiniquities), unless God shall give them Repentancerepentance for them, for the which I pray with all my heart.

310309. But that which was reported with the boldest confidence, was, that I had my Missesmisses, my Whoreswhores, my Bastardsbastards, yea, two Wiveswives at once, and the like. Now these slanders (, with the other), I glory in, because but slanders, foolish, or knavish lies, and falshoodsfalsehoods cast upon me by the Devildevil and his Seedseed,; and should I not be dealt with thus wickedly by the Worldworld, I should want one sign of a Saintsaint, and Childchild of God.. ‘ Blessed are you (said the Lord Jesus) when men shall revile youyou, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil of you faslyfalsely for my sakesake; rejoice, rejoice and be exceeding glad, for great is your Rewardreward in Heavenheaven; for so persecuted they the Prophetsprophets which were before youyou’ (Matt 5:11, Mat. 5. 1112).

311310. These thingsthings, thereforetherefore, upon mine own accountaccount, trouble me not,; no, though they were twenty times more than they are. I have a good Conscienceconscience;, and whereas they speak evil of me, as an evil doer, they shall be shamedashamed that falsely accuse my good Conversationconversation in Christ.

312311. SoSo, then, what shall I say to those that have thus bespattered me? Shall I threaten them? Shall I chide them? Shall I flatter them? Shall I entreat them to hold their Tonguestongues;? noNo, not I, were it not for that these things make them ripe for damnationdamnation, that are the Authorsauthors and Abettorsabettors, I would say unto them;, Report it? becauseBecause twill, because it will increase my Gloryglory.

313312. Therefore I bind these lies and slanders to me as an ornament, it belongs to my Christian Profession,profession to be vilified, slandered, reproached, and reviled; and since all this is nothing else, as my God and my Conscienceconscience do bear me witness:, I rejoycerejoice in reproaches for ChristsChrist’s sake.

314313. I also calling all these fools, or knaves [, that have thus made it any thinganything of their business to affirm any of the things afore-named of me, namely, that I have been naught with other Womenwomen, or the like. When they have used to the utmost of their
endeavours, and made the fullest enquiryinquiry that they cancan, to prove against me trulytruly, that there is any Womanwoman in Heavenheaven, or Earthearth, or Hellhell, that can say, that I have at any time, in any place, by day or night, so much as attempted to be naught with themthem; and speak I thus, to beg mine Enemiesenemies into a good esteem of me:? No, not I: I will in this beg belief of no man:; believe, or disbelieve me in this, all is a case to me.

315314. My Foesfoes have mistmissed their mark in this their shooting at me. I am not the manman. I wish that they themselves be guiltless,. ifIf all the Fornicatorsfornicators and Adulterersadulterers in England were hang’dhanged by the Neckneck till they be deaddead, John Bunyan, the object of their Envyenvy, would be still alive and well. I know not whether there be such a thing as a Womanwoman breathing under the Copescopes of the whole Heavenheaven but by their Apparelapparel, their Childrenchildren, or by common Famefame, except my Wifewife.

316315. And in this I admire the Wisdomwisdom of God, that heHe made me shieshy of Womenwomen from my first Conversionconversion until now,. Those know, and can also bear me witness, with whom I have been most intimately concerned, that it is a rare thing to see me carry it pleasant towards a Womanwoman;, the -common Salutationsalutation of Womenwomen I abhor,’ it tisis odious
to me in whomsoever I see it. Their Companycompany alonealone, I cannot away with. I seldom so much as touch a Womanswoman’s Handhand, for I think these things are not so becoming me. When I have seen good men Salutesalute those Womenwomen that they have visited, or that have visited them, I have at times made my objection against it, and when they have answeredanswered, that it was but a piece of Civilitycivility, I have told themthem, it is not a comely sight:; some indeed have urged the holy kiss,; but then I have asked why they made baulks, why they did salute the most handsomhandsome, and let the illill- favoured go? thusThus; thus, how laudable so eversoever such things have been in the Eyeseyes of others, they have been unseemly in my sight.

317316. And now for a wind up in this matter, I calling not only Menmen, but Angelsangels, to prove me guilty of having carnally to do with any Womanwoman save my Wifewife, nor am I afraid to do it a second time, knowing that it cannot offend the Lord in such a case, to call God for a Recordrecord upon my Soulsoul, that in these things I am innocent. Not that I have been thus keptkept, because of any goodness in me, more than in any other,
but God has been merciful to meme, and has kept me,; to whom I pray that heHe will keep me still, not only from thisthis, but from every evil way and work, and preserve me to hisHis Heavenlyheavenly Kingdomkingdom. Amen.

318317. Now as SathanSatan laboured by reproaches and slandersslanders, to make me vile among my Country-mencountrymen, that, if possible, my Preachingpreaching might be made of none effect, so there was added hereto a long and tedious Imprisonmentimprisonment, that thereby I might be frighted from my Serviceservice for Christ, and the Worldworld terrified, and made afraid to hear me Preachpreach, of which I shall in the next place give you a brief account.

div.head: A brief Account of the Authors Imprisonment.
div.p:
319318. Having made Professionprofession of the Gloriousglorious Gospelgospel of Christ a long time, and Preachedpreached the same about five years;, I was apprehended at a Meetingmeeting of good Peoplepeople in the CountreycountryCountry,
(among whom, had they let me alone, I should have preached that day, but they took me away from amongst them), and had me before a Justicejustice; who, after I had offered security for my appearing at the next Sessionssessions, yet committed me, because my Suretiessureties would not consent to be bound that I should Preachpreach no more to the Peoplepeople.

320319. At the Sessionssessions after, I was indicted for an Upholderupholder and Maintainermaintainer of Unlawfulunlawful Assembliesassemblies and Conventiclesconventicles, and for not Conformingconforming to the Nationalnational Worshipworship of the Church of England;, and after some Conferenceconference there with the Justicesjustices, theythey, taking my plain dealing with them for a Confessionconfession, as they termed it, of the Indictmentindictment, did Sentencesentence me to perpetual banishment, because I refused to Conformconform. SoSo, being again delivered up to the Goalersgaolers’ hands, I was had home to Prisonprison, and there have lain now compleatcomplete twelve years, waiting to see what God will suffer these men to do with me.

321320. In which condition I have continued with much contentcontent, through Gracegrace, but have met with many turnings and goings upon my Heartheart, both from the Lord, Satan, and my own Corruptionscorruptions; by all
which (, glory be to Jesus Christ)! I have also received, among many things, much Convictionconviction, Instructioninstruction, and Understandingunderstanding, of which at large I shall not here discoursediscourse; onelyonly give youyou, in a hint or twotwo, a word that may stir up the Godlygodly to bless God, and to pray for me; and also to take encouragement, should the case be their own, Notnot to fear what man can do unto them.

322321. I never had in all my life so great an in-letinlet into the Word of God as now them Scriptures; those scriptures that I saw nothing in before, are made in this place and state to shine upon me; Jesus Christ also was never more real and apparent than now; here I have seen himHim and felt himHim indeed: O. Oh! that word, We have not preached unto you cunningly devised Fablesfables, ( 2 Pet. 1.: 16. andAnd), and that, God raised Christ from the Deaddead;, and gave him Gloryglory, that your-Faith faith and Hopehope might be in God. ( 1 Pet. 1. 2. wereWere:21), were blessed words unto me in this my imprisoned Conditioncondition.

323322. These three or four Scripturesscriptures also have been great refreshment, in this condition, to me? ( John 14.: 1, 2,–4; 16:33; Col 3: 3, 4 John 16. 33. Col. 3. 3, 4.; Heb. 12.: 22, 23,– 2424). So that sometimes, when I have been in the savour of them, I have been able to
laugh at destruction, and to fear neither the Horsehorse nor his Riderrider (Job 39:18). I have had sweet sights of the forgiveness of my Sinssins in this place, and of my being with Jesus in another World: Oworld. Oh! the Mount Sion, the heavenly Jerusalem, the innumerable Companycompany of Angelsangels, and God the Judgejudge of all, and the Spiritsspirits of Justjust men made perfect, and JesusJesus (Heb 12:22–24), have been sweet unto me in this place:. I have seen that here, that I am perswadedpersuaded I shall never, while in this Worldworld, be able to express;: I have seen a truth in that Scripturescripture,, ‘ Whom having not seen, yetye love; in whom, though now you see him notnot, yet believing, yet rejoycerejoice with ioyjoy unspeakable, and full of Gloryglory’. ( 1 Pet. 1.: 88).

324323. I never knew what it was for God to stand by me at all turns, and at every offer of Satan to afflict me, &etcc. as, asAs I have found himHim since I came in hither;: for look how fears have presented themselves, so have supports and encouragements; yea, when I have started, even as it were, at nothing else but my shadow, yet God, as being very tender of me, hath not suffered me to be molested, but wouldwould, with one Scripturescripture or anotheranother, strengthen me against all; insomuch that I have often said, Were it lawful, I could pray for greater
trouble, for the greater comfortscomfort’s sake, ( Eccl. 7.: 14.; 2 Cor. 1.: 55).

325324. Before I came to Prison,prison I saw what was a coming, and had especially two Considerationsconsiderations warm upon my heart; the first was, Howhow to be able to endure, should my imprisonment be long and tedious; the second was, how to be able to encounter Deathdeath, should that be here my portion,. For the first of these, that Scripturescripture, ( Col. 1.: II11.) waswasWas great information to me, namely, to pray to GodGod, ‘ to be strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and long-suffering with joyfulness;.’ I could seldom go to prayer before I was imprisoned, but for not so little as a year together, this Sentencesentence or sweet Petition,petition would, as it were, thrust it selfitself into my mind, and perswadepersuade me, that if ever I would go thorowthrough longlong- suffering, I must have all patience, especially if I would endure it joyfully.

326325. As to the second Considerationconsideration, that Saying, (2 Cor. 1. 9.)saying was of great use unto me,, ‘ But we had the sentence of death in our selvesourselves, that we might not trust in our selvesourselves, but in God that raiseth the deaddead’ (2 Cor 1::9). By this Scripturescripture I was made to see that, That if ever I would suffer rightly, I must first pass a sentence of death upon every thingeverything that can properly be called a thing of this life,
even to reckon my selfmyself, my Wifewife, my Childrenchildren, my Healthhealth, my Enjoymentsenjoyments, and all, as dead to me, and my selfmyself as dead to them.

327326. The second was, to live upon God that is invisible;, as Paul said in another place,; Thethe way not to faint, is to look‘Look not at the things that are seen, but at the things that are not seen;: for the things that are seen, are temporal,; but the things that are not seen, they are eternaleternal’ (2 Cor 4::18). And thus I reasoned with my self; ifmyself, If I provide only for a Prisonprison, then the Whipwhip comes at unawaresunawares, and so doth also the Pillorypillory:. Again, if I provide only: for these, then I am not fit for banishment;: further, if I conclude that banishment is the worst, then if Death come,death comes I am surprizedsurprised;: so that I seesee, the best way to go thorowthrough sufferings is to trust in God through Christ, as touching the Worldworld to come; and as touching this Worldworld, to count the Gravegrave my Househouse, to make my Bedbed in Darknessdarkness,; to say to Corruptioncorruption, Thou art my Fatherfather, and to the Wormworm, Thou art my Mothermother and Sistersister;: that is, to familiarize these things to me.

328327. But notwithstanding these helps, I found my selfmyself a man, and compassed with Infirmitiesinfirmities; the parting with my Wifewife and poor Childrenchildren hath often been
to me in this place, as the pulling the Fleshflesh from my Bonesbones;, and that not only because I am somewhat too fond of these great Merciesmercies, but also because I should have often brought to my mind the many hardships, miseriesmiseries, and wants that my poor Familyfamily was like to meet with, should I be taken from them, especially my poor blind Childchild, who lay nearer my heart thenthan all I had besides; O. Oh! the thoughts of the hardship I thought my blind one might go under, would break my heart to pieces.

329328. Poor Childchild! thoughtthoughtThought I, what sorrow art thou like to have for thy Portionportion in this Worldworld?! Thou must be beaten, must beg, suffer hunger, cold, nakedness, and a thousand Calamitiescalamities, though I cannot now endure the Windwind should blow upon thee:. But yet recalling my selfmyself, thought I, I must venture you all with God, though it goeth to the quick to leave you;. OOh,! I saw in this condition, I was as a man who was pulling down his Househouse upon the head of his Wifewife and Childrenchildren; yet thought I, I must do it, I must do it:. And now I thought of those two Milch-Kinemilch kine that were to carry the Arkark of God into another Countrycountry, and to leave their Calvescalves behind them, ( 1 Sam. 6.: 10, 11,– 1212).

330329. But that which helped me in this temptation, was divers considerations, of which three in special here I will name;: the first was, the consideration of those two Scripturesscriptures,, ‘ Leave thy Fatherlessfatherless Childrenchildren, I will preserve them alive, and let thy Widowswidows trust in me: and.’ And again,, ‘ The Lord said, Verily it shall go well with thy Remnantremnant, verily, I will cause the Enemyenemy to entreat thee well in the time of evil,’ &c.( Jer. 49.: 11. Chap.; 15. II:11).

331330. I had also this Considerationconsideration, that if I should now venture all for God, I engaged God to take care of my concernments;: but if I forsook himHim and hisHis ways, for fear of any trouble that should come to me or mine;, then I should not only falsifiefalsify my profession, but should count also that my Concernmentsconcernments were not so sure, if left at GodsGod’s feet, whilst I stood to and for hisHis Namename, as they would be if they were under my own care, though with the denial of the way of God. This was a smarting consideration, and was as spurs unto my Fleshflesh:. That Scripturescripture also greatly helped it to fasten the more upon me where Christ prays against Judas, that God would disappoint him in all his selfish thoughts, which moved him to sell his
Mastermaster. Pray read it soberly, Psal(Ps. 109.: 6, 7, 8, &etc.–20)c.

332331. I had also another Considerationconsideration, and that was, The the dread of the Tormentstorments of Hellhell, which I was sure they must partake of, that for fear of the Crosscross do shrink from their Professionprofession of Christ, hisHis words and Lawslaws, before the Sonssons of men:; I thought also of the Gloryglory that heHe had prepared for those that in Faithfaith, and Lovelove, and Patiencepatience, stood to hisHis ways before them,. These things, I say, have helped me, when the thoughts of the misery that both my selfmyself and mine, might, for the sake of my Professionprofession, be exposed to, hath lain pinching on my Mindmind.

333332. When I have indeed conceited that I might be banished for my Professionprofession, then I have thought of that Scripturescripture,, ‘ They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain with the Swordsword;: they wandered about in Sheep-Skins,sheepskins and Goat-Skins,goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented,; ( of whom the Worldworld was not worthyworthy)’ (Heb 11:37,, 38); for all they thought they were too bad to dwell and abide amongst them. I have also thought of that saying;, ‘ The Holy Ghost witnesseth in every Citycity,,’ ‘ that Bondsbonds and Afflictionsafflictions abide me;’ (Acts 20:23). I have verily thought that my Soulsoul and it,
have sometimes reasoned about the sore and sad estate of a banished and exiled condition, how they are exposed to Hungerhunger, to Coldcold, to Perilsperils, to Nakednessnakedness, to Enemiesenemies, and a thousand Calamitiescalamities; and at lastlast, it may bebe, to die in a Ditch,ditch like a poor forlorn and desolate Sheepsheep. But I thank God hitherto I have not been moved by these most delicate reasonings, but have ratherrather, by themthem, more approved my Heartheart to God.

334333. I will tell you of a pretty business;: I was once above all the rest, in a very sad and low Conditioncondition for many Weeksweeks,; at which time alsoalso, I being but a young Prisonerprisoner, and not acquainted with the Lawslaws, had this laylying much upon my Spiritspirit, Thatthat my Imprisonmentimprisonment might end at the Gallowsgallows for oughtaught that I could tell;. nowNow therefore Satan laid hard at meme, to bear me out of heart, by suggesting thus unto me;, But how ifif, when you come indeed to diedie, you should be in this Conditioncondition; that is, as not to savour the things of God, nor to have any evidence upon your Soulsoul for a better state hereafter? (for indeed at that time all the things of God were hid from my Soulsoul.)

335334. Wherefore when I at first began to think of this, it was a great trouble to me:; for I thought with my selfmyself, that in the Conditioncondition I
now was in, I was not fit to die, neither indeed diddid I think I could if I should be called to it:; Besidesbesides, I thought with my selfmyself, if I should make a scrambling shift to clamber up the Ladderladder, yet I shouldshould, either with quaking or other symptoms of fainting, give occasion to the Enemyenemy to reproach the Wayway of God and his People,His people for their Timorousnesstimorousness. ThisThis, thereforetherefore, lay with great trouble upon me, for methought I was ashamed to die with a pale Faceface, and tottering Kneesknees, for such a Causecause as this.

336335. Wherefore I pray’dprayed to God that heHe would comfort me, and give me strength to do and suffer what heHe should call me to; yet no comfort appear'dappeared, but all continued hid:; I was also at this time so really possessed with the thought of death, that oft I was as if I was on a Ladderladder with the Roperope about my Neckneck; only this was some Encouragementencouragement to me, I thought I might now have an opportunity to speak my last words to a Multitudemultitude, which I thought would come to see me die; and thought I, if it must be so, if God will but convert one Soulsoul by my very last words, I shall not count my Lifelife thrown away, nor lost.

337336. But yet all the things of God were kept out of my sight, and still the Temptertempter followed me with, But whither must you go when you die? Whatwhat will become of you? Wherewhere will you be found in another Worldworld? Whatwhat evidence
have you for Heavenheaven and Gloryglory, and an Inheritanceinheritance among them that are sanctified? Thus was I tossed for many Weeksweeks, and knew not what to do; at last this Considerationconsideration fell with weight upon me, Thatthat it was for the Wordword and way of God that I was in this Conditioncondition,; wherefore I was engaged not to flinch an hairshair’s breadth from it.

338337. I thought also, that God might chusechoose whether heHe would give me comfort now, or at the hour of Deathdeath; but I might not therefore chusechoose whether I would hold my Professionprofession or no:; I was bound, but heHe was free,; yea,’ twas ’twas my Dutyduty to stand to hisHis Wordword, whether heHe would ever look upon me or save me at the last: Wherefore,wherefore thought I, save the point being thus, I am for going on, and venturing my eternal Statestate with Christ, whether I have comfort here or no;. ifIf God doth not come in, thought I, I will leap off the Ladderladder even blindfold into Eternityeternity, sink or swim, come Heavenheaven, come Hellhell;, Lord Jesus, if thouThou wilt catch me, do; if not, I will venture for thyThy Namename.

339338. I was no sooner fixed upon this Resolution,resolution but that word droptdropped upon me, Doth Job serve God for nought? As if the Accuseraccuser had said, Lord, Job is no upright
Manman, he serves thee for by Respects-respects;: Hasthast thou not made an Hedgehedge about him, &etcc.? butBut put forth now thine Handhand, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy Faceface. How now, thought I, is this the sign of an upright Soulsoul, to desire to serve God when all is taken from him;? Is he a godly Manman that will serve God for nothing rather than give out? Blessed be God; Thenthen I hope I have an upright Heartheart, for I am resolved (, God giving me strength), never to deny my Professionprofession, though I have nothing at all for my Painspains;: and as I was thus considering, that Scripturescripture was set before me, Psal(Ps. 44.: 12. &etc.–26)c.

340339. Now was my Heartheart full of Comfortcomfort, for I hoped it was sincere;: I would not have been without this Tryal,trial for much; I am comforted every time I think of it, and I hope I shall bless God for ever for the teaching I have had by it. Many more of the dealings of God towards me, I might relate., Butbut thesethese, out of the spoils won in Battelbattle, have I dedicated to maintain the Househouse of God, ( 1 ChronChr 26:27). 26, 27..

div.p: 1. OFOf all the Temptationstemptations that ever I met with in my Lifelife, to question the Beingbeing of GodGod, and Truthtruth of hisHis Gospelgospel, is the worst, and worst to be borne; when this Temptationtemptation comes, it takes away my Girdlegirdle from me, and removeth the Foundationfoundation from under me:. OOh, I have often thought of that word,, ‘ Have your Loynsloins girt about with Truthtruth’:; and of that,, ‘ When the Foundationsfoundations are destroyed, what can the Righteousrighteous do??’

2. Sometimes, whenwhen, after sin committedcommitted, I have looked for sore Chastizementchastisement from the Handhand of God, the very next that I have had from himHim hath been the discovery of hisHis Gracegrace. Sometimes, when I have been comforted, I have called my selfmyself a Foolfool for my so sinking under trouble. And thenthen, againagain, when I have been cast down, I thought I was not wise to give such way to comfort. With such strength and weight have both these been upon me.

3. I have wondredwondered much at this one thing, that though God doth visit my Soulsoul with never so blessed a discovery of himselfHimself, yet I have found again, that such
hours have attended me afterwards, that I have been in my Spiritspirit so filled with darkness, that I could not so much as once conceive, what that God and that comfort was with which I have been refreshed.

4. I have sometimes seen more in a line of the Bible, then than I could well tell how to stand under, and yet at another time the whole Bible hath been to me as dry as a stick; or ratherrather, my Heartheart hath been so dead and dry unto it, that I could not conceive the least dram of Refreshmentrefreshment, tho’though I have look'tlooked it all over.

5. Of all fears, they are best that are made by the Bloodblood of Christ; and of all Joyjoy, that is the sweetest that is mixtmixed with mourning over Christ:. Oh! 'it tisis a goodly thing to be on our kneesknees, with Christ in our Armsarms, before God. I hope I know something of these things.

6. I find to this day seven Abominationsabominations in my Heart;heart: ( 1.) Inclinings to Unbeliefunbelief.. ( 2.) Suddenly to forget the Lovelove and Mercymercy that Christ manifesteth.. ( 3.) A leaning to the Worksworks of the Lawlaw.. ( 4.) WandringsWanderings and coldness in Prayerprayer.. ( 5.) To forget to watch for that I pray for.. ( 6.) Apt to murmur because I have no more, and yet ready to abuse what I have.. ( 7.) I can
do none of those things which God commands me, but my Corruptionscorruptions will thrust in themselves., ‘ When I would do good, evil is present with me. 7’

7. These things I continually see and feel, and am afflicted and oppressed with,; yet the Wisdomwisdom of God doth order them for my good.. ( 1.) They make me abhor my selfmyself.. ( 2.) They keep me from trusting my Heartheart.. ( 3.) They convince me of the Insufficiencyinsufficiency of all inherent Righteousnessrighteousness.. ( 4.) They shewshow me the Necessitynecessity of fleeing to Jesus.. ( 5.) They press me to pray unto God.. ( 6.) They shewshow me the need I have to watch and be sober.. ( 7.) And provoke me to pray unto GodGod, through ChristChrist, to help me, and carry me through this Worldworld.. Amen.
